decision: Activate the already selected rpylean repair with exact source and Arena candidate identities, fixed dependent and recursive controls, and no external-write authority. Baseline reproduction, runtime setup, implementation, upstream validation, local review packet, main-only delivery and successor selection are one item.

categories.assessment: Implementation against the kernel-derived rule construction is more useful than another known-case screen; the bounded question is whether a complete ordinary-rule comparison can reject the published wrong argument without rejecting valid dependent or recursive controls.

Exact upstream source, Arena blobs and prospective controls are bound. The repair will retain before/after evidence, supported-shape limits and a reusable upstream regression; unrelated historical custody gaps remain out of scope.
The selected work has a concrete rpylean maintainer consumer and a public false-proof boundary. It may prepare, but not submit, a pull-request packet.

Reuse Lean's official mk_rec_infos and mk_rec_rules construction as the semantic source and Arena #350 as prior exposure. Do not infer authority from checker consensus or build a general cross-checking package.
The missing PyPy/RPython runtime is a feasible setup task inside the item. No scientific input, permission or external dependency blocks activation.

candidates.rationale: Selected highest-value feasible item: it can turn a public semantic defect into a source-derived checker repair, direct regression and maintainer-ready local patch.
Standalone reproduction adds insufficient value; its baseline is incorporated into the repair.
It remains available but has no demonstrated decision-changing need and does not repair the live boundary.
No demonstrated consumer need or incremental regression value.
